links.outcome: Fracture detection specificity of ChatGPT-5 on hip radiographs (false positives) as standalone diagnostic
links.effect: IT femur: 100% sensitivity but only 16.7% specificity (κ = 0.24); hallucinated fractures in normal hip X-rays; proximal humerus 87.5% sensitivity, 100% specificity (κ = 0.74).
links.quote: However, limitations in specificity and fine-detail recognition restrict its autonomous clinical use.

links.outcome: False-positive fracture detection by AI on normal hip radiographs
links.effect: ChatGPT-5 had 16.7% specificity in IT femur fractures and frequently hallucinated fractures in normal hip X-rays.
links.quote: While it identified major fracture patterns and comminution reliably, it frequently hallucinated fractures in normal hip X-rays and missed fine details such as lesser tuberosity fragments and dislocations.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the diagnostic performance of a multimodal LLM (ChatGPT-5) on retrospective radiographs against expert ground truth without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
